intro: The Daodejing is one of the most translated books in the world. Yet no one knows for sure who wrote it. For centuries, readers had only copies passed down by hand. Then, in 1973 and 1993, archaeologists opened tombs and found copies more than 2,000 years old.

In this unit you will look at the evidence about Laozi, the Daodejing and the Zhuangzi. You will compare old manuscripts and see why translation is hard. Then you will meet Daoism as a living religion, with its Celestial Masters, deities, canon, priests, temples, immortals and practices.

By the end, you will be able to explain how scholars date and compare manuscripts. You will be able to tell the Daodejing from the Zhuangzi by genre. And you will be able to describe Daoist religious life accurately and respectfully.
bigQuestion: What are the Daoist texts, where did they come from, and how does Daoism live as a religion today?

test.q: Who wrote the oldest biography of Laozi?
test.why: Sima Qian's Shiji (c. 94 BCE) contains the oldest account.

test.q: What do the Guodian slips show?
choices: Parts of about 31 chapters in a different order
test.why: The Guodian bamboo, c. 300 BCE, holds parts of about 31 chapters.

test.q: What order do the Mawangdui copies use?
test.why: Both silk copies put the De half before the Dao half.

test.q: What does Daodejing ch. 1 say about the Dao?
choices: The Dao that can be trodden is not the enduring Dao
test.why: Legge's ch. 1 says the Tao that can be trodden is not the enduring and unchanging Tao.

test.q: Which book contains the butterfly dream?
test.why: The butterfly dream ends chapter 2 of the Zhuangzi.

test.q: Which statement about the Zhuangzi is correct?
choices: Its seven inner chapters are thought closest to Zhuangzi
test.why: Scholars treat the inner chapters 1–7 as closest to Zhuangzi's thought.

choices: Classical Chinese is brief and words like dao have many meanings

test.q: In which year do Daoists date Zhang Daoling's revelation?
test.why: Daoist tradition dates the revelation from Lord Lao to 142 CE.

choices: The Daoist canon of about 1,400 texts
test.why: The Daozang, printed 1445, is the Daoist canon.

test.q: How do religious Daoists honor Laozi?
test.why: Religious Daoists honor Laozi as Most High Lord Lao.
He Xiangu is shown with a lotus.
Qigong means working with qi through breath and movement.

test.q: Which view do many scholars now hold about the two Daoisms?
test.why: Many scholars see philosophical and religious Daoism as one tradition.

test.q: Which sentence is written as a scholar would?
choices: Daoists believe their rites bring blessing to the community.
test.why: Attributing a belief describes it without judging it.

write.prompt: What can manuscripts tell us about the Daodejing? Cite Daodejing ch. 1 or ch. 8 (Legge, 1891), the Mawangdui and Guodian finds, and one Zhuangzi story (Legge, 1891). Explain what scholars conclude and how Daoist readers view Laozi's authorship.
tips: Name each text, chapter and translation you cite.
Attribute each view to scholars or to Daoists.
Describe differences between copies without calling one 'wrong.'
Use unit words like manuscript, received text and hypothesis.
